audience: People evaluating, operating, or extending the CMS, including non-developers who need precise behavior without implementation noise.
cadence: Lead with the outcome. Keep paragraphs short, define terms on first use, and use ordered steps for state-changing workflows.
claim_policy: State verified behavior as fact. Label planned, approval-gated, or unverified behavior explicitly. Never imply that a successful publish is already live before production confirmation.
cta_policy: Calls to action should name the next safe operation and its effect, such as reading a contract, validating a draft, or releasing a tested batch.

frameworks.description: Explain the model, why it exists, and how its parts relate.
frameworks.label: Concept explanation
frameworks.when_to_use: Use when the reader needs a mental model before operating the feature.

frameworks.description: Guide a reader through a state-changing workflow with gates and recovery points.
frameworks.label: Operational runbook
frameworks.when_to_use: Use for publishing, tenant creation, deployment, and incident recovery.

name: Platform documentation voice
reader_safety_notes: Keep credentials, internal strategy annotations, private review notes, and implementation-only secrets out of reader-visible copy.
